title: What decides your finish date?
principle: Find the critical path. Buy ready-made anything that could make you late.

screens.text: Let me tell you about the Delhi Metro. In India, big building projects were often years late. But the Delhi Metro finished its first part two years and nine months ahead of time, in 2005, and within its budget. Have a guess how.

screens.prompt: What do you think helped the Delhi Metro finish so early?

options.label: It ran its sites day and night
It built everything itself, from day one
It tracked deadlines, day by day

screens.why: Its chief, E. Sreedharan, tracked every deadline day by day. And rather than wait to learn to build trains, it bought the first ones ready-made from South Korea. Later trains were finished in India by BEML, an Indian company.

screens.title: The critical path
screens.text: Here's how to find what decides your date. Some jobs wait for others: buy flour, then bake, then pack. That's a chain. The longest chain is your critical path. Speed up any other job, and you finish the same day. If a job on it is slow, buy it ready-made.

screens.title: Now look at your bakery
screens.text: A metro and a wedding cake both have a date that can't move. It's November, your home bakery's fifth year, and the wedding season. A family wants a three-tier cake and 200 cupcakes for 28 November. Some jobs can happen side by side, while others must wait.

screens.prompt: Chain 1: stands from Mumbai, 10 days. Chain 2: design approval, 3 days, then test cake, 2 days. Both run together. Which sets your date?

options.label: Chain 2: design and test cake, 5 days

screens.why: Exactly. Both chains run side by side, so the longer one decides: 10 days for the stands. That's your critical path. Rushing the test cake won't bring the wedding cake one day closer.

wrong.a: Chain 2 takes 3 + 2 = 5 days, but the stands take 10. Both run at the same time, so the longer chain, 10 days, decides your date.
wrong.c: You'd add them only if one had to wait for the other. These run side by side, so the longer chain decides: 10 days for the stands.

screens.prompt: Check your past orders: stands from Mumbai took 10, 12 and 13 days. The shop says 10. How many days do you plan for?
screens.why: Right. A writer, Douglas Hofstadter, made this a law: things take longer than you plan, even when you plan for delay. Plan for the slowest time you've seen, and add spare days if you can.

wrong.a: That's the shop's promise. But they took 10, 12 and 13 days before. Plan for the slowest, 13 days.
wrong.b: 12 days would have been late one time in three. They took up to 13 days before, so plan for 13. Things take longer than you plan.

screens.prompt: Here are five steps for planning a big order, mixed up. Put them in the right order.
steps: List every job the order needs
Mark which jobs must wait for another
Add up the days in each chain of jobs
Find the longest chain: your critical path
Add spare days, and buy ready-made anything that could make you late
screens.why: Exactly. You can't find the longest chain until you know every job and which ones wait for others. Then add spare days, because things take longer than you plan, and buy ready-made anything on the critical path that could make you late.

screens.setup: It's 15 November. The wedding is in 13 days. Cake stands from Mumbai cost ₹900 and took 10 to 13 days before. No shop nearby sells them, but one rents them today for ₹1,500, ₹600 more than Mumbai.
screens.question: How do you plan the wedding order?

options.label: Order from Mumbai, and bake the cupcakes early
options.outcome: The cupcakes are ready by 20 November. The stands arrive on the 27th, the night before. By then the cupcakes are a week old, and you bake all 200 again, about ₹3,000 more, while decorating three tiers all night.
options.why: You sped up a job that wasn't on the critical path, so the finish date didn't move. The stands were the long chain.
options.better: Rent the stands nearby today, and buy your own later.

options.label: Order from Mumbai, and save ₹600
options.outcome: The stands arrive on day 12, the evening before the wedding. You decorate through the night. The cake is ready, but one tier leans, and you fix it at the hall an hour before the guests arrive.
options.why: You saved ₹600, but you left no spare days on your slowest job, and it came close to making you late.
options.better: Rent the stands nearby today, and buy your own later.

options.label: Rent stands nearby today, for ₹600 more
options.outcome: You have the stands today. The test cake is done by the 20th and the family approves it. You bake the cupcakes two days before, and the cake is ready a day early. In January, with no rush, you order your own stands from Mumbai.
options.why: Exactly. You paid ₹600 to take the slowest job off the critical path, with spare days left. Buy ready-made anything that could make you late, and make it yours later.

screens.prompt: One more thing: the family will pay ₹18,000. You spend ₹8,000 on flour, boxes and stands first. What should you ask for?

options.label: Half now, half on the day
All of it after the wedding
Give them ₹2,000 off to pay now

screens.why: Right. Half now is ₹9,000, enough to cover the ₹8,000 you spend first. Remember the gym deal from Unit 1: before a big order, check how much cash you'll have before the customer pays.

wrong.a: Then you spend ₹8,000 of your own cash first, and wait to be paid. Remember Unit 1: ask for an advance. Half now, ₹9,000, covers the ₹8,000.
wrong.c: That costs you ₹2,000 you don't need to lose. An ordinary advance, half now, is ₹9,000, enough for the ₹8,000 you spend first.

screens.text: Chain A takes 7 days. Chain B takes 4, then 3, then 1. They run together. The critical path is chain ___, taking ___ days.
screens.why: Exactly. Chain B is 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 days, longer than A's 7. That's your critical path. Plan spare days on it, and buy ready-made anything on it that could make you late.

summary: Critical path: the longest chain of jobs that must wait for each other. It sets your finish date.
Speeding up a job off the critical path doesn't move the finish date.
Hofstadter's law: things take longer than you plan. Add spare days, and buy ready-made anything that could make you late.

cards.front: Job A takes 8 days. Jobs B then C take 3 and 2 days. They run side by side. When can you finish?
cards.back: The longest chain decides: 8 days. That's the critical path.

cards.front: A part from far away may make you late. What should you do?
options: Buy or rent it nearby, and make it yourself later
cards.back: Buy ready-made anything that could make you late.

cards.front: A job took 4, 5 and 7 days before. How long do you plan?
cards.back: Hofstadter's law: it always takes longer than you expect.

sources.label: A well-planned and efficient Delhi Metro: tracing 16-year journey (ThePrint)
